wpa_supplicant: fix the constant roaming problem We saw that on certain platforms in certain places we keep switching between two APs and eventually get the same RSSI. Debugging showed that we have a very big difference between the two antennas. Ant A can hear AP A very well (-60) but AP B very bad (-80) Ant B can hear AP B very well (-60) but AP A very bad (-80) When the device associates to AP A, it'll learn to use Ant A. If the device uses one single antenna to receive the scan results, it may hear the AP it is currently associated to on the second antenna and get bad results. Because of that, the wpa_supplicant will roam to the other AP and the same scenario will repeat itself: Association to AP A (Ant A reports -60). Scan on Ant A: AP A: -60, AP B: -80 Scan on Ant B: AP A: -80, AP A: -60 ==> ROAM. Association to AP B (Ant B reports -60) Scan on Ant A: AP A: -60, AP B: -80 ==> ROAM Etc... Fix this by querying the signal of the current AP using drv_signal_poll() instead of relying on the signal that we get from the scan results. BUG=b:111071506 TEST=Modify the driver to lie about the RSSI with the patch below. Then, setup two APs with the same SSID: one on channel 1 and one on channel 6 and check if we keep bouncing between the two APs. diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/rx.c b/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/rx.c index 593b0ed..59296e1 100644 --- a/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/rx.c +++ b/drivers/net/wireless/intel/iwlwifi/mvm/rx.c @@ -168,11 +168,18 @@ static void iwl_mvm_get_signal_strength(struct iwl_mvm *mvm, energy_c = (val & IWL_RX_INFO_ENERGY_ANT_C_MSK) >> IWL_RX_INFO_ENERGY_ANT_C_POS; energy_c = energy_c ? -energy_c : S8_MIN; + + if (le16_to_cpu(phy_info->channel) == 1) + energy_a -= 30; + + if (le16_to_cpu(phy_info->channel) == 6) + energy_b -= 30; + max_energy = max(energy_a, energy_b); max_energy = max(max_energy, energy_c); - IWL_DEBUG_STATS(mvm, "energy In A %d B %d C %d , and max %d\n", - energy_a, energy_b, energy_c, max_energy); + IWL_DEBUG_STATS(mvm, "energy In A %d B %d C %d , and max %d channel %d\n", + energy_a, energy_b, energy_c, max_energy, le16_to_cpu(phy_info->channel)); rx_status->signal = max_energy; rx_status->chains = (le16_to_cpu(phy_info->phy_flags) & Change-Id: I21090246c6943c9ba57f2961c013246b835daa3a Signed-off-by: Emmanuel Grumbach <emmanuel.grumbach@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1201583 Commit-Ready: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org> Tested-by: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org>

[autotest] iw_runner: fix get_regulatory_domain() with new 'iw' 'iw reg get' changed format a bit last time we upgraded it. Now it includes a 'global' section heading, like this: global country US: DFS-UNSET (2402 - 2472 @ 40), (N/A, 30), (N/A) (5170 - 5250 @ 80), (N/A, 17), (N/A) (5250 - 5330 @ 80), (N/A, 23), (0 ms), DFS (5490 - 5730 @ 160), (N/A, 23), (0 ms), DFS (5735 - 5835 @ 80), (N/A, 30), (N/A) (57240 - 63720 @ 2160), (N/A, 40), (N/A) This causes our naive parsing to choke (and we fail network_WiFi_RegDomain everywhere), since we only capture something at the very start of the string. Extend our rule to do a proper multiline search, and just take the first result. BUG=none TEST=network_WiFi_RegDomain Change-Id: I11b4b8de5473937ee8df04a7463c976d512be0ac Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1196773 Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org>
